facts.label: Told me + would
facts.sub: Para contar uma promessa ou plano, use told me + would + verbo: He told me he would be late. Sem pessoa, use said: He said he would come.

facts.label: Planos no passado
facts.sub: Quando contamos uma promessa, will vira would: “I will help” vira “He said he would help.” O verbo seguinte continua na forma base: would come, would call, would be.

facts.label: Disse a mim
facts.sub: Use told + pessoa + frase: He told me he would be late. He told us he would call. Não use said me. Se não houver pessoa, use said: He said he would be late.

compare.ask: He told me he would be late.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “ele disse que chega às dez” e o verbo muda pouco.
compare.tip: Diga: “He told me he would be late.”
compare.us: Em inglês, will vira would: “He said he would arrive at ten.” Com pessoa, use told: He told me he would come.

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.

extra90: Dupla: um fala como no Brasil, o outro como nos EUA.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Would is the past form of will in reported speech.
“I will call” becomes “He said he will call.”
items.why: Usually: He said he would call.

items.s: Told needs a person: told me, told us.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Would is the past form of will in reported speech. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
“I will call” becomes “He said he will call.” → Falso (Usually: He said he would call.)
Told needs a person: told me, told us. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A snowy morning · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a cold Monday morning in an office in Denver. Snow covers the cars outside the building. Edith checks the clock on the wall. The room is almost empty. Her coworker Luisa walks in with a coffee. Edith asks where the manager is.
“Luisa, where is the manager? The meeting starts in ten minutes.” says Edith. “He told me he would be late because of the snow.” says Luisa. “Did he tell you how late he would be?” says Edith.
